proposals.title: Lower bound ssat(n, C5) >= 11n/8 - O(1) (Fueredi-Kim Conjecture 4.1)
proposals.literal_quantifiers: Conjecture (record text): 'The minimum number of edges in an n-vertex C5-semisaturated graph satisfies ssat(n,C5) = 11/8 n + O(1).' Scope: all n (asymptotic statement as n -> infinity). Definition: G is C5-semisaturated iff for every non-edge e of G, G+e has strictly more C5 copies than G.
proposals.definitions: C5-semisaturated (Fueredi-Kim arXiv:1103.0067): adding any missing edge increases the number of 5-cycles. Equivalent reformulation used throughout: every non-adjacent pair {u,v} is joined by a path of length 4 with three internal vertices (a C5 through uv in G+uv is uv plus a 4-path from v to u). ssat(n,H) = minimum number of edges of an n-vertex H-semisaturated graph.

source_evidence.item: furedi-kim-1103.0067v1-cycle-saturated.pdf retained in sources/ (sha256 1f049570ebbe0fbc760c0b6eb964044869bf74184ede791c91f8db78482df4ea); Conjecture 4.1 reads 'ssat(n,C5) = 11/8 n + O(1). Maybe equality holds in (6) for n > n0.' with (6): 'ssat(n,C5) <= ceil(11/8 (n-1)) for all n >= 5.'

state_of_art.upper_bound: Fueredi-Kim construct C5-semisaturated graphs on 8t+1, 8t+3, 8t+5, 8t+7 vertices with 11t, 11t+3, 11t+6, 11t+9 edges and extend to even n by pendant-edge removal; conjectured optimal.
state_of_art.open_part: The lower bound ssat(n,C5) >= 11n/8 - O(1). Only the general-cycle bounds (Theorem 4.2: (1+1/(2k-2))n - 2 < ssat(n,Ck) for n >= k >= 6) exist, which for k=5 does not apply and gives nothing near 11/8.
state_of_art.small_n_discrepancy: EXHAUSTIVE dual-checked computation in this lane gives exact values ssat(5)=6, ssat(6)=8, ssat(7)=9, while (6) at n=6 reads ceil(11*5/8)=7: the published small-n claim (6) FAILS at n=6 (no 7-edge C5-semisaturated graph on 6 vertices exists; verified by two independent definitions over all 23,832 graphs n in {5,6}, m<=8). The hypothesis delegate must resolve this against the published version - it may be a v1 typo or affect the conjectured O(1).

proposals.mechanism: Full-scope lower-bound proof plan. (1) Structure: a C5-semisaturated graph is connected (vertices in different components have a non-edge with no 4-path) and every non-edge spans a 4-path. (2) Block decomposition: analyze leaf blocks B with cutvertex c. For u in B\{c}, any w outside B: the 4-path from u to w must pass through c, so B must contain, for each such u, a u-to-c path of length 2 or 3, or c must have a suitable 2-path into B - this forces end-block density. Target lemma: every end-block satisfies e(B) >= (11/8)(|B|-1) - C, and internal blocks satisfy e(B) >= (11/8)|B| - C, with the constants absorbed by the finitely many end blocks (giving the O(1)). (3) Discharging: assign to each vertex v charge e-charge minus 11/8 and discharge along 4-path witnesses; the minimal counterexamples should concentrate deficit on degree-2 vertices of path-like end blocks, which the FK gadget avoids by using 8-vertex blocks with 11 edges. (4) The FK 8-vertex gadget must be reverse-engineered from the paper's figure (n=1+7t... on page 5 region; the v1 text extraction shows a 7-vertex 10-edge picture - clarify) and verified semisaturated by the retained checker.

Outputs in work/ssat_c5_smalln.out and work/ssat_c5_crosscheck2.out.

proposals.certificate_size_and_formal_interfaces: Lean endpoint: definition of semisaturation (forall non-edge, exists 4-path with distinct internal vertices), the exact small-n enumeration lemmas (decidable, finite), and the discharging lower bound. Estimated 800-1500 lines; only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound. The finite enumeration can be certified by reflection on the explicit witness/countermodel lists. No sorry/axiom/unsafe/native_decide.
proposals.classical_adaptation_objection: The statement is already purely finite/combinatorial (no asymptotic analysis is classical-hostile), so there is no classical-adaptation objection to the STATEMENT; the objection is mathematical: an O(1) claim must control the constant, and the n=6 discrepancy shows the O(1) term is nonzero and sign-sensitive (ssat(6)=8 > 6.875). If the true answer were ssat(n,C5) = 11n/8 + c with c ~ n^0.5 for some family, the conjecture fails; the delegate must first push the exact computation to n=9,10 to see the error term trend before attempting the discharge.
proposals.risk: Medium. The lower bound may need genuinely new structural ideas beyond leaf-block discharging; no dedicated prior-art sweep has been done.

proposals.title: Finite coloring of Sturmian factors forcing every factorization to change color
proposals.literal_quantifiers: Given a Sturmian word W: does there exist a finite non-empty color set C and a coloring c: F+(W) -> C such that for EVERY factorization W = U_0 U_1 U_2 ... (U_i in F+(W) nonempty, concatenation = W) there exist indices i != j with c(U_i) != c(U_j)? If so, what is the smallest |C|? Scope: for every Sturmian word W (all irrational slopes), plus the minimum-cardinality question.
proposals.definitions: F+(W) = set of non-empty finite factors of W. Factorization = decomposition of the infinite word into consecutive non-empty factors. A factorization is monochromatic (for color class S) if all blocks have the same color. Reformulation: a monochromatic factorization of color class c^{-1}(gamma) is an infinite path 0 = p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < ... in the directed graph on N with edge p -> q (q > p) iff c(W[p:q)) = gamma.

source_evidence.item: Record statement from the hash-verified corpus extract (Oberwolfach Reports 10.4171/OWR/2010/37, page 48, year 2010). The originating talk and speaker were NOT identified; the OWR page itself is behind ems.press and was not fetched.

prior_evidence.finding: No direct hit for the exact problem in bounded search (combinatorics on words niche). Known adjacent facts used: Sturmian words are aperiodic, balanced, uniformly recurrent; the gap sequence of each letter takes exactly two values {m, m+1} and is aperiodic. No claim of exhaustive clearance.

dedup_evidence.finding: Not in coverage-delta.json, accepted-exclusions.json, or historical-dispositions.json; not among credited first-batch families.

proposals.mechanism: Two-sided resolution plan. NEGATIVE SIDE (no coloring exists): for every finite coloring c, construct a monochromatic factorization. Key reduction: an infinite monochromatic factorization exists iff for some color gamma and block-length bound B there are monochromatic-gamma factorizations of prefixes W[0:M] with all blocks <= B for unbounded M (Koenig, after bounding block lengths; the raw tree is infinitely branching and Koenig fails without the bound). Then use Sturmian structure: positions of any letter are syndetic (gaps in {m, m+1}); represent boundaries by their rotation point x_p = {p*alpha} and reduce the path existence to reachability in a finite graph of interval-exchange states (Rauzy induction on the return-word decomposition); aperiodicity blocks the only periodic obstructions. POSITIVE SIDE (a coloring exists): if the negative side fails, exploit aperiodicity to build c from the two gap values, e.g. color by (first letter, length, and the position of the factor inside its return-word context) and verify via the same finite graph that no monochromatic path survives; then minimize |C| by trying k = 2, 3, ....

decisive_bounded_calculation.run_here: work/sturmian_mono_factorization_dp.py (run under guard, outputs in work/sturmian_mono_factorization_dp.out): on a 10^6-letter Fibonacci word prefix, EVERY color class of the naive family c(U) = (first letter, |U| mod k), k = 2..6, admits monochromatic boundary paths reaching the end of the prefix (furthest boundary 999990..999999), while classes with first letter '1' are unreachable from position 0 (W[0]='0'). This eliminates the entire naive family and shows any working coloring must be content-sensitive beyond first-letter/length data.
decisive_bounded_calculation.planned: (a) Extend the DP to track (position mod M, prefix-parity state) to confirm the same failure for automaton-style colorings (a 4-state check was verified by hand for (|U| mod 2, #1s mod 2): mono factorization exists because both state components are syndetic). (b) Implement the finite interval-exchange graph for the Fibonacci slope and decide the existence question exactly for the Fibonacci word; then generalize via continued-fraction induction. PLANNED, not run.

proposals.certificate_size_and_formal_interfaces: Lean endpoint: for a FIXED slope (e.g. Fibonacci word defined via the standard morphism), a decidable finite-graph statement; the full-scope 'for every Sturmian word' version needs the continued-fraction induction formalized or an explicit coloring with a hand proof. Estimated 600-1200 lines for the fixed-slope negative resolution; the all-slopes version is larger. Only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound.
proposals.classical_adaptation_objection: The statement is combinatorics on words - already classical. The objection is scope: 'every Sturmian word' is a family parameterized by irrational alpha; a proof for the Fibonacci word does NOT resolve the record. Any full-scope proof must be uniform in alpha (or the positive coloring must be constructed for all alpha), and the minimal-|C| part needs a matching lower-bound argument over all colorings. If the delegate can only settle fixed slopes, the outcome must be reported as partial and receives no full-scope credit.
proposals.risk: Medium-high. The negative side (no coloring exists) is plausible - every natural coloring tried admits a monochromatic factorization - but a general proof needs a genuinely new compactness/syndeticity argument; the positive side would be surprising.
